data.text/markdown:
Day-start forecast

Does a Darts model have an edge over pure luck at one question: at a fixed time of day, will the stock be up or down at the end of the horizon, and by roughly how much?
  • one example = one stock-day: the model reads the history before the decision and predicts the bars to the end of the horizon; the tuning grades only the move to the end
  • one stock at a time (SYMBOLS): now DOCN (DigitalOcean), the most movement among the names with full 1-minute data since January 2025; the first runs used COLB
  • the optimizer searches the history length, the inputs and the model (Tables 1 and 7); everything else is fixed (Table 2)
  • the luck check: every score is compared with random up/down outcomes of the same sizes

Settings

The next cell holds every setting, in six blocks. Edit a value and everything below re-runs.
  1. The question (fixed): when the prediction is made, and how far ahead it looks
  2. The data: the stock, TEST (read once, at the very end, in both modes) and WALK_FORWARD, which picks ONE of two ways to learn and score:
    • 2a · single split (WALK_FORWARD = False): one model learns on TRAIN and scores all of VALIDATION
    • 2b · walk-forward (WALK_FORWARD = True): WF_SCORED is cut into steps (a month or a week, WF_STEP); each step is scored by its own model, which learns on the WF_WINDOW_MONTHS months just before that step (a rolling window, as a model retrained live; None: every earlier day), then everything moves one step on
Only the chosen block is used; Table 4 and Figure 0 show its exact days
  1. What the optimizer searches: the history length and the inputs (Table 1); the model types and their knobs are in Table 7
  2. Training (fixed): how many passes, when to stop
  3. The luck check: how many random outcomes every score is compared with
  4. The worked example: one configuration for "What goes in" and "Train one model"

data.text/markdown:
Words
  • decision / horizon: when the prediction is made, and how far ahead it looks (both fixed: they define the question)
  • input: the minutes of history the model reads before the decision (searched)
  • bar: minutes of trading, built from the stored 1-minute bars
  • typical move: a bar's move ÷ the usual size of that clock time's move (last 20 sessions), so calm and wild stocks are comparable
  • end move: the stock's total move from the decision to the end of the horizon, in typical moves: what the tuning grades
  • end-move correlation: how well predicted and actual end moves line up over all VALIDATION stock-days (the tuning's score; 0 = no skill)
  • luck z: how many luck-widths the end-move correlation sits above random up/down outcomes of the same sizes (about 2 = rare by chance for ONE try; the best of many tries needs more)
  • R² vs "no change": 0 = as good as saying nothing, above 0 = better (the path grade of the worked example)

Stocks and the data split

The days are loaded and cut as set in block 2. Table 4 and Figure 0 show, for the chosen mode, one row per model (a single split has one, walk-forward one per scored month) and TEST:
  • history only: the first 10 sessions; the typical sizes need earlier sessions, so these days are read, never learned
  • learns: the model's training days; its last 10 are held out to stop the training and to set the size scale β
  • scores: the days its predictions are graded on; all models' scored days together give a trial its score
  • TEST: read once, at the very end
With walk-forward, each model learns on the WF_WINDOW_MONTHS months just before its step and scores that step; then everything moves one step on, as a model retrained live (with None, each model learns on every earlier day). Half-days (13:00 close) are never used.

data.text/markdown:
Tune: Optuna searches, W&B records

run the studies runs one study per model type of MODEL_TYPES (Table 7) and horizon (Table 2), up to MAX_TRIALS trials each. Every trial answers the same question: decide at the fixed time, predict the stock's move to the end of the horizon. A trial draws the history length and the inputs (Table 1) and the model type's knobs (Table 7), trains, and is graded on VALIDATION.
  • score (maximized): the end-move correlation: how well predicted and actual moves to the end of the horizon line up over all VALIDATION stock-days. It is scale-free: a confident model is not punished for its size, a quiet line earns nothing
  • luck check: every trial's correlation against DRAWS make-believe outcomes with the same sizes and random up/down (luck_z, luck_p; hit_p for the hit rate). The best of many trials needs a higher z: the line above Table 8 gives the bar
  • also per trial: hit rate (right up/down), the size error after a scale β learned on the held-out days (mae_skill: 1 − error ÷ the "no change" error), the end R², and every stock's own correlation (the worst stock, the share of stocks above 0)
  • loss: a searched knob: bar (every bar's move, Darts' default) or endpoint (only the move to the end, what the score cares about)
  • walk-forward (WALK_FORWARD = True, block 2b): each step of WF_SCORED is scored by its own model, which learns on the window just before that step (Table 4, Figure 0): one fit per step per trial, its own studies ("wf" in the name). The section Compare sets both modes side by side, on the days both score
  • no pruning: every trial trains until its own early stopping (PATIENCE); each pass's held-out R² is still reported (Figure 5, Optuna Dashboard)
  • studies: journals in studies/, one per model type and horizon, named by a fingerprint of every setting; re-running tops each up to MAX_TRIALS. Each trial's predictions are saved in var/daystart_trials/ (re-scoring needs no retraining)
  • W&B: one run per trial through OptunaHub's W&B callback, grouped by study: the knobs, the scores, every stock's correlation and the per-pass curve. Offline in var/wandb/ (WANDB_MODE=offline in .env)
  • compare: Table 8 (the best of each model type and horizon), Table 9 (all trials), Table 10 and Figure 7 (the best trial, per stock and per stock-day), Figures 4–6 (the study of the best trial)
  • caveat: VALIDATION is one month; the best of many trials is partly luck. Read the winner on TEST once, at the end

data.text/markdown:
Compare: single split vs walk-forward

Table 11 puts each model type's study in both modes side by side (a mode that has not run yet is missing). The two modes may score different days (VALIDATION, WF_SCORED), so every trial is also re-scored, from its saved predictions, on the days both modes score: those columns and Figure 8 compare like for like.
  • the best trial: its end correlation and luck z, against the bar the best of that many trials reaches by luck alone; above the bar = more than luck
  • all trials: the median end correlation and the share of trials above luck (z ≥ 2) say more than one lucky best
  • months positive: in how many VALIDATION months the best trial's correlation is above 0; an edge that lives in one month is fragile (trials scored before this column existed show "–")
